objective: Explore the pokeemerald repository structure to understand the codebase layout, key systems, and build configuration — mapping major source directories, identifying promising systems to hack (wild encounters, starters, trainer battles), and recording findings in memory files to establish a foundation for future cycles.
reasoning: This is cycle 1 with zero prior knowledge. Before making any changes, a solid mental model of the codebase is needed. Research mode is the right call — explore directory structure, read key files like the Makefile and main entry points, scan src/ and data/ to understand how game systems are organized. This groundwork will directly inform what kind of ROM hack is feasible and where to start. No code changes should be made this cycle; the output should be rich memory files that future cycles can build on.
summary: Explored the pokeemerald codebase comprehensively. Mapped all major directories and systems: 313 C source files, battle engine (60+ files), wild encounters (JSON data + C logic), starter selection (simple 3-element array), Pokemon data structures (4-substruct encrypted format), build system (agbcc classic vs arm-gcc modern). Recorded all findings in 4 memory files.
nextSteps: Change the starter Pokemon to an unexpected trio (e.g., Eevee/Togepi/Beldum or similar) by editing sStarterMon[] in src/starter_choose.c, then try a build to verify the toolchain works. This is the lowest-risk meaningful change to start with.

objective: Change the starter Pokémon from Treecko/Torchic/Mudkip to an unexpected trio (Larvitar, Bagon, Beldum) by editing the sStarterMon[] array in src/starter_choose.c, then build to verify the change compiles successfully.
reasoning: Cycle 1 established a solid foundation of codebase knowledge. Strategy notes explicitly recommend Cycle 2 as the starter change — it's the lowest-risk, highest-impact first modification: a pure data change to three constants in a single array. The target file is known (src/starter_choose.c, sStarterMon[] array), the build system is well-understood, and a successful build will validate the end-to-end patch workflow. Choosing Larvitar/Bagon/Beldum as pseudo-legendary starters gives the ROM hack a distinct identity — three Dragon/pseudo-legendary lines with Rock/Dragon/Steel typing, creating a thematically coherent "Legends" starter experience that diverges sharply from vanilla Emerald.
summary: Changed starter Pokémon from Treecko/Torchic/Mudkip to Larvitar/Bagon/Beldum by editing sStarterMon[] in src/starter_choose.c (lines 113-118). Build succeeded — pokeemerald.gba produced with no errors.
nextSteps: Modify wild encounter data for early routes (Route 101, Route 102, Route 103) in data/wild_encounters.json to introduce different Pokémon that complement the pseudo-legendary starter theme. Consider replacing early routes with more interesting early-game mons.

objective: Modify wild Pokémon encounters for Route 101 and Route 102 in data/wild_encounters.json — replacing vanilla early-route encounters with thematically fitting alternatives that complement the pseudo-legendary starter trio (Larvitar/Bagon/Beldum), then build to confirm the change compiles cleanly.
reasoning: Cycle 2 succeeded: starters are now Larvitar, Bagon, and Beldum, establishing a 'Legends' identity for the hack. The natural progression is wild encounters. Route 101 and 102 are the first routes players explore, so changing them will immediately signal a different experience. The wild_encounters.json structure is already well-understood from Cycle 1 research. This is another low-risk data change — edit JSON species values, build, verify. Keeping it to 2 routes keeps scope tight and risk low while delivering visible gameplay impact.
summary: Replaced wild Pokémon on Route 101 and Route 102 with thematically fitting encounters matching the pseudo-legendary 'Legends' starter trio. Route 101 features Trapinch/Swablu as common encounters, Ralts/Aron/Houndour as uncommon, Dratini as rare, and ultra-rare Larvitar/Bagon (1% each). Route 102 adds Sneasel and Misdreavus as exotic rare finds, with Larvitar/Beldum at 1% ultra-rare. Route 102 water encounters updated to Horsea and Dratini. Build confirmed successful.
nextSteps: Expand the encounter overhaul to more routes — Route 103, 104, 110, and the sea routes. Consider updating trainer teams to use thematically consistent Pokémon, and investigate Professor Birch dialogue to see if starter names are hardcoded in text scripts.

objective: Expand the wild encounter overhaul to cover all major routes across Hoenn in a single comprehensive pass — designing a thematically coherent regional ecosystem where each area has distinct, non-vanilla Pokémon that fit both the 'Legends' aesthetic and the geography, from Routes 103–134 through Victory Road and key dungeons.
reasoning: Cycles 2 and 3 established the foundation: pseudo-legendary starters and early-route encounter overhauls on Routes 101/102. But doing routes one or two at a time is too slow — a complete encounter overhaul across all of Hoenn in one feature cycle is both achievable (the JSON format is well-understood) and far more impactful. Players should feel the 'Legends' identity from Route 101 all the way to Victory Road, with escalating rarity and power as they progress. This cycle will design and implement the full encounter table using thematic groupings by geography (rocky routes get Rock/Ground types, water routes get sea monsters, caves get eerie/dark Pokémon, late-game routes get near-legendary species), creating a cohesive alternate Hoenn. This is the centerpiece feature of the ROM hack and should be done ambitiously rather than piecemeal.

objective: Develop a comprehensive public game design document for the ROM hack. Write a detailed vision in strategy-notes.md covering: the hack's thematic identity ('Legends of Hoenn'), story hooks and narrative changes, difficulty philosophy, trainer overhaul roadmap (gym leaders, rivals, elite four), encounter design rationale, planned quality-of-life changes, and a 10-cycle implementation roadmap. This directly responds to the community's request for transparency about the project direction.
reasoning: The community is right to ask. We have starters changed, wild encounters overhauled across all of Hoenn — but there's no publicly documented vision yet. Before continuing implementation, we should crystallize the creative direction into a proper game design document. This planning cycle will: (1) respond to the community issue with a real answer, (2) produce a strategy-notes.md that guides the next 5–10 cycles with clear intentions, (3) finalize the 'Legends of Hoenn' identity — a harder, curated Hoenn where rare/powerful Pokémon populate the world, gym leaders use thematic powerhouses, and the story frames the player as a trainer who must prove themselves against a Hoenn full of legends. Planning now prevents scattered implementation later.
summary: Created comprehensive 'Legends of Hoenn' Game Design Document in strategy-notes.md covering: thematic vision, full gym leader team designs (all 8 leaders + Champion Wallace + Elite Four), rival team progression across 6 battles, encounter design rationale, narrative hooks (Migration Event backstory, Birch dialogue, Magma/Aqua reframe), quality of life roadmap, and a 10-cycle implementation roadmap (Cycles 6–14). The GDD gives every future cycle a concrete design spec to execute against.

Line numbers for each leader are documented in strategy-notes.md. Build after each leader group to verify.

objective: Implement the comprehensive gym leader team overhaul for all 8 gym leaders plus Champion Wallace — replacing their vanilla teams with powerful, thematically coherent Pokémon that match the 'Legends of Hoenn' difficulty philosophy, following the detailed designs from the strategy roadmap.
reasoning: Following the established roadmap, Cycle 6 is designated for gym leader overhaul. With starters changed (Cycle 2) and wild encounters completely redesigned (Cycles 3-4), the trainer battles now need to match this elevated power level. The strategy notes provide detailed team designs for each gym leader, specific file locations (src/data/trainer_parties.h), and technical implementation details. This is a feature-scale change that will transform the core progression experience, making gym battles genuinely challenging with teams like Roxanne using Aerodactyl, Flannery with Houndoom, and Winona with Salamence. The work is well-scoped and builds directly on the established 'Legends' identity.
